https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Sample-Shadows-120x-zoom.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] While Magic Capture took most of the spotlight in Google’s keynote, maybe the most discussed photo upgrade this year is Camera Looks. I did a whole interview with Google’s camera chief about this feature going deep into how the new system was made, and there’s a lot of potential in the execution. Camera Looks is a new photography feature you can think of similar to Fujifilm’s film simulations, which let its cameras emulate different film styles on the JPGs they put out. On the Pixel 11 series, there are four modifications of the standard camera, with Original, Natural, Shadows, and Vanilla giving subtle tweaks to your image. But if you want to get more out there, there are six additional creative looks, called Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie, and Minimal. Each of the looks can be modified to your liking, with adjustable settings like contrast, highlights, shadows, vibrance, tint, warmth, sharpness, and grain. What makes this a really interesting feature to me is that Google is adjusting the amount of computational processing it’s doing at capture, based on the settings you choose; it’s not just applying filters later. For example, the Digi mode will do less frame stacking and the Minimal mode will apply less sharpness and contrast. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-9.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-8.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-6.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-5.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Camera-Looks-Sample-3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-Black-Tie-Camera-Look.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] I really dig the looks, even right out of the box. They span from basic edits to quite inspired, and if you’re looking for something that gives you the “film simulation look” straight out of camera, these definitely deliver. It was high time Google added some more creative looks to the Pixel, especially considering it doesn’t have nearly as robust a third-party camera ecosystem as the iPhone. I’ve personally made the Minimal mode permanent on my phone for its unsharpened, minimally contrasty look, occasionally switching to Classic, but after testing them all, I think Velvet and Editorial will get a lot of use, since they have the most “film aesthetic” of the bunch. With less processed photos, you can actually see texture in photos, which is normally washed away by noise reduction algorithms. Overall camera quality on the Pixel 11 Pro series is great this year, and practically the only reason to pick up a Pro Pixel over the standard 11, aside from wanting a larger phone, in the case of the XL. The primary sensor is technically new, but Google tells me it’s the same size as last year and was swapped in because it uses slightly less power. The biggest camera hardware change is the new larger telephoto sensor, which Google says captures more light, and I can tell. Telephoto cameras are usually the weakest link in a smartphone’s camera arsenal, but even at 10x zoom, which is a 2x crop of the telephoto sensor, it was hard to notice any significant quality degradation. Plus, the transition between sensors is much smoother now, with only a very slight jump when switching between lenses. [Image: The Camera Looks interface. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Taking-Photo-Camera-Looks-Velvet.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The Pixel 11 Pro also includes a 120x Pro Zoom mode, enabled by the new image signal processor in Tensor G6. Like the 100x Pro Zoom on the Pixel 10 Pro, Google is using generative AI to upscale your highly zoomed-in images to make them look more realistic. On objects without a lot of sharp edges this actually does a pretty good job, and Google will give you both the non-AI-enhanced and enhanced versions so you can see the difference. I was in Spain during last week’s solar eclipse, and the Pixel 11 Pro did a good job of turning a zoomed-in photo of the moon from a blurry mess into something that looked good enough to elicit responses of awe when I posted it in Slack. But that was a relatively simple image, and shots with a lot more detail often look like an early AI-generated image, with skewed angles and edges, garbled text, and muddy tones. I’d only really use this if you needed to see information you can’t see with your normal eyes, not for artistic purposes. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-Super-Res-Zoom-100x.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-Super-Res-Zoom-120x.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The Pixel 11 Pro also gets a new, faster Night Sight, which Google says is about three times faster on average than the Pixel 10 Pro. In testing, most Night Sight images I took only needed to be held for one second, and I got all the same benefits you got from holding the phone for three or more seconds previously. This is the kind of quality-of-life update I love to see, and I’m glad Google is continuing to improve here. I love Rambler, Magic Capture, and Camera Looks. If you’re looking to upgrade your phone this year, they’re legitimately great features. But after a week of use, it’s clear to me that the Pixel 11 Pro is not yet smart enough to help me use my phone less, despite what Google claims. Proactive Assistance is only bound to save you a few seconds and a few taps compared to just opening the apps and doing the steps yourself. If you were hoping for the Pixel 11 Pro would help address your phone addiction, that’s probably not going to happen. But if you’re looking for a phone with the best voice-to-text on the market, great cameras with good built-in style, and solid hardware, the Pixel 11 Pro delivers.  Photography by David Imel / The Verge

articles.title: Somehow, Despite Being the Sixth Film in the Franchise, Insidious: Out of the Further Delivers a Popcorn-Rattling Ride Full of Fun, Creative Scares
articles.summary: Insidious: Out of the Further delivers a popcorn-rattling ride full of fun, creative scares and serviceable human stakes that more than justify tiptoeing through the tulips back to the spirit world.
articles.body:
Insidious: Out of the Further is in theaters on Friday, August 21.

With 2023’s Insidious: The Red Door having served as an effective swan song to Blumhouse’s first original horror franchise, Out of the Further arrives with one chance to prove that the light over the series’ spectral crimson door deserves to be kept on after all. With a grab bag of different-flavored scares that broadly work, some grounded performances, and a willingness to double down on the abject weirdness of the world-building that’s been established up to this point, against the odds for a sixth film in any franchise, Insidious: Out of the Further maintains a steady stride and winds up being a hell of a good time.

As the title suggests, Insidious: Out of the Further sets itself apart from the films which precede it by opening the proverbial (and literal) door from the spirit realm into the material plane in a much more significant way than ever before. It’s true that we’ve seen the spirits of the Further out in the real world, but generally, these apparitions are fairly closely shackled to the bodies of those they’re trying to possess, and incapable of too much more than going “boo”... or I guess luring them into the street, like in the case of Insidious: Chapter 3 ’s Quinn. The particulars of how (and to what degree) the Further gets Out are fun to discover along the way, but suffice to say that protagonist Gemma (Amelia Eve) had a rough childhood that has left her unable to move on in life in a way that’s made her a valuable target for the spirits of The Further. The opening scene paints a truly sad picture of Gemma’s childhood, as she tiptoes around her house to avoid drawing the attention of her mother, who’s clearly in the throes of a crisis that’s been going on for some time. It sets up a dynamic that carries into Gemma’s adulthood, as she navigates fears of transferring that experience onto her daughter Maya (Island Austin).

Amelia Eve does fine work shouldering Gemma’s growing instability as she tries to keep her feet on the ground, although writer/director Jacob Chase’s script hammers a bit too hard on the “passing familial trauma along” element of the story, routinely saying out loud what the imagery and performance already clearly communicate. It feels especially repetitive in the context of Insidious: The Red Door’s plot, which focused on the reconciliation of Patrick Wilson and Ty Simpkins’ Josh and Dalton Lambert after their shared experiences in the first two chapters of the series. Though it’s not always subtle, Chase does at least prioritize threading that family drama through Out of the Further in a way that keeps the central wound Gemma is nursing in focus, so that her desperation remains palpable throughout. We see the past repeating itself through Maya’s eyes as Gemma unravels, and Island Austin strikes a good balance between vulnerability and tenacity through her mom’s ups and downs.

Given all the new facets of how the Further is able to interact with the material plane in this film, Chase is able to stage a number of creative and fresh scenarios that delight in blurring the line between what’s happening in reality and what’s bleeding over from the spirit realm. Chase knows the Insidious films well, capably easing into the visual language of the series while also having a keen sense of how the rhythms of encounters with the denizens of the Further are expected to play out. At worst, the scares work about as well as they have in any other Insidious film (jump scares and audio stings abound), but Chase brings no shortage of new ideas to the table.

Two strong back-to-back sequences around the film’s midpoint represent Out of the Further at its best. The first is a claustrophobic’s nightmare set in Maya’s pillow fort. As Gemma pokes her head in, the pillow fort becomes a rat’s maze in which she’s very much not alone. Chase is able to draw the tension out of every wrong turn through the labyrinth very effectively, including some fun misdirects and camera coverage that make the most out of the tight space. By the time Gemma finally emerges, the viewer should feel just as relieved as the character.

But it’s the following sequence, which follows Gemma to her job as a dental hygienist, that is Out of the Further’s crown jewel. For a franchise that has always forefronted spectral spookies and haunted house-style bumps in the night, Insidious: Out of the Further features one of the more disgusting and visceral dental horror scenes I can recall ever having seen, as Gemma goes to work on a guy who seems like he may be better off getting his teeth checked by the Lipstick Face Demon from the first movie. Chase draws this sequence out to a fever pitch, layering one sickening and all-too-realistic gag over another. All that really dampens this excellent sequence is how it tails off into the Further, where evil-looking dentists and patients seem far more tame than the actual oral horror we just witnessed out in the real world.

The Insidious films have favored vague, elemental demons as antagonists up to this point, really as more of a visual focal point for the sleepless evil contained in the Further, but Out of the Further makes the smart choice to try out a more well-drawn villain this time out, played by A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms’ Sam Spruell. Cyrus Lam is no hoofed, red-faced Beelzebub, but a cunning spirit with an interesting backstory which connects to how much more interaction the Further and the real world have this time out. Cyrus and his motives aren’t all that deep, but he’s different enough from previous antagonists to make his moves feel a lot more unpredictable.

Out of the Further’s strength at delivering on that namesake concept does belie a weakness of the film’s, which is that most of the material set in the Further itself is rather forgettable. The space tends to be a VFX-darkened/color-graded void in the shape of whatever house or neighborhood that particular movie is set in, where the spirits have greater power. On that front, we’re pretty firmly in “been there, done that” territory. Die-hards will no doubt delight in the myriad familiar faces among the vaudevillian freakshow of ghouls that call the Further home, but with the stakes of the film being so focused on preventing the Further from getting out, much of the anxiety surrounding the idea of the characters being trapped within feels too distant for those moments to feel all that weighty.

The movie’s supporting cast are uniformly strong at keeping Insidious: Out of the Further from astral projecting itself into incoherence. Is there anything new for Lin Shaye’s Elise Rainier to do here other than amend exposition from previous movies to explain new abilities, raise a lantern in the darkness of the Further, and scream at ghosts in the face after dying five movies ago? Nope. Is her presence and personality as welcome and warm a blanket as ever? You betcha. As Gemma’s boyfriend Nick, Brandon Perea and his excellent comedic timing are particularly well-deployed as a very open-minded skeptic. Legends of Tomorrow’s Maisie Richardson-Sellers stops by as tattoo artist/medium Clare to pick up the torch from Elise in the material plane, and while she’s mostly there as a conduit for Elise, it’s easy to see her steely comfort with the abnormal becoming a more prominent part of the series going forward. And a special shoutout to the pair of actors who play Gemma’s neighbors, the O’Sullivans. They (with some canny direction on Chase’s part) absolutely nail a self-referential gag during the very intense finale and give me hope that, for every 10 or 12 poe-faced entities that reoccur from previous movies in future installments, we get one appearance from these two just doing their best to be helpful and not to bicker too much while doing so.

articles.title: GTA VI keeps leaking ahead of its gameplay premiere
articles.summary: Clips of what appears to be Grand Theft Auto VI have hit the internet, possibly spoiling aspects of the game ahead of Rockstar Games’ deep dive. Some clips have already been pulled.
articles.body: Clips of what appears to be Grand Theft Auto VI have hit the internet, possibly spoiling aspects of the game ahead of Rockstar Games’ deep dive debuting on Netflix next week and its long-awaited launch in November. I’ve seen three clips seemingly showing off the game, though two have been pulled from the site I saw them on “due to a copyright claim.” The first clip (now removed) was a quiet scene that mostly focused on Jason Duval, one the game’s two protagonists, shooting a basketball into a hoop. Another clip (also removed) featured more of the crime-focused gameplay you’d expect from GTA, including Duval hitting a person with a wrench, and also showed the return of a six-star Wanted system. A third clip, which is live as I write this, shows Duval driving at night, punching some people, using a taser, and stealing a truck. The clip then jumps to what looks like a cutscene from a different part of the game in the daytime. The videos were watermarked by a person or group identifying themselves as “CyberLeek.” The third clip has a call for viewers to buy a CyberLeek cryptocurrency, a QR code, links to some sketchy-looking CyberLeek URLs, and a statement that says “NO PHYSICAL DISCS? THEN MORE LEEKS!”, which is seemingly a reference to Rockstar’s decision not to launch GTA VI on a physical disc. This isn’t the first time apparent footage from GTA VI has leaked. In 2022, 90 videos leaked online long before the game’s official reveal more than a year later (a reveal that also leaked, leading Rockstar to publish the game’s first trailer a day early). A teen who played a key role in leaking the 90 videos was sentenced to life in a secure hospital. Rockstar also confirmed earlier this year that it had data compromised in a hack of a third-party provider, but said the incident would have “no impact on our organization or our players.” Rockstar and owner Take-Two didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. The GTA VI “extended look” premieres on Netflix on August 27th at 3PM ET and will stream on YouTube at 9PM ET. The $79.99 title is scheduled to launch on November 19th, and for the most part, the industry is steering clear of November and launching their big games earlier in the year.

articles.title: The Witcher 3 NPCs Kept Dropping Their Babies Due to an Unintended Side Effect of a Cut Mechanic
articles.summary: The Witcher 3 developers were so focused on making a realistic environment for players that they accidentally created a morbidly hilarious side effect for the game’s female NPCs.
articles.body:
The Witcher 3 developers were so focused on making a realistic environment for players that they accidentally created a morbidly hilarious side effect for the game’s female NPCs.

In an interview with Edge Magazine , CD Projekt Red quest designer Philipp Weber opened up about the unintended consequences of this strategy, saying the team was so honed in on creating a believable world that they ended up causing chaos, instead.

Weber explained that they wanted to give NPCs authentic behaviors to increase immersion and reward players for exploring the nooks and crannies of The Continent, particularly where small villages in the countryside were concerned.

"Because we were focused on the countryside, it was easier for players to become curious," he began. "If a village only has eight houses, people will want to see if the people truly exist in the world, or if it's just fakery. Lots of people nowadays are interested in those kinds of details, and it really came to haunt us."

At the time, Weber said the dev team was "more focused on simulating their proper day and night cycle" for these NPCs rather than giving them believable reactions to Geralt as he wandered around their world. “When it came to actually reacting to the player, there wasn't that much detail,” he admitted.

This meant that, although the NPCs had their own highly-specific schedules that made them seem like living, breathing people going about their daily lives, they weren’t exactly logical when it came to Geralt barging into their homes and swinging his weapons around.

"They would drop what they're currently working on, that thing would fall to the ground, and they'd run away, afraid,” Weber said.

Unfortunately (or fortunately, since it’s objectively funny) those ‘things’ included babies, which female characters would throw to the floor as they fled from danger. "For a few weeks, women were just dropping their babies, left and right,” he said.

While this problem ended up getting solved, it would have been absolutely wild to see in the final product. Weber shed a bit more light on their strategy when making NPCs in general, saying that rather than giving them specfic instructions, they're able to choose from certain "spots of interest."

"Most NPCs in villages, we don't give them specific paths," he explained. "We give them spots of interest that are available and then they're the ones doing the pathfinding: 'Once I'm done with woodcutting, I'll choose another point, and maybe do carpentry in front of my house'. For the 50 sailors at Novigrad harbour, for example, we made 200 possible spots, so even if all 50 were active at the same time, they would have options."

The next entry in the Witcher series is currently in development. Centering on Ciri, it does not yet have an official release date, but early gameplay footage was shown off for the State of Unreal 2025 showcase. We can’t imagine NPCs will be tossing their babies in this game, either, but you never know. (It certainly wouldn't be wilder than the 'put the baby in the oven' option.)

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Wolverine: Origin III Explores Marvel's Controversial Prequel Arc
articles.summary: Marvel is wading into controversial waters again with Wolverine: Origin III - The Dark Age, the latest chapter in the dramatic origin story of the iconic X-Man.
articles.body:
Before the release of 2001's Wolverine: Origin, it was unthinkable that Marvel would ever reveal the full background and origin story of the enigmatic man known as Logan. That book revealed Wolverine's true name (James Howlett) and explored the tragic series of events that led to him becoming an orphaned loner. It also directly inspired the 2009 movie X-Men Origins: Wolverine. Now Marvel is continuing that controversial saga with a third chapter called Wolverine: Origin III - The Dark Age.

Wolverine: Origin III - The Dark Age brings back original Origin writer Paul Jenkins. The series is illustrated by CAFU (Venom). Issue #1 features a main cover by Wes Burt and a variant cover by Josemaria Casanovas.

Origin III jumps further ahead in the Marvel timeline. Whereas the original was set in late 19th century Canada and 2013's Origin II was set in the early 20th century, Origin III takes place after World War II. After years spent waging war, Logan has finally found some semblance of peace, but will his past come back to haunt him?

Enter the Dark Age! After years of trauma and back-to-back tours of duty fighting in the first two World Wars, Logan has found his new mission…peace! With his berserker rage and violent tendencies somehow behind him, Logan enjoys a new life of tranquility and service. Logan will meet new friends and allies, and with the help of an impassioned young doctor, discover what makes him tick. But what is the cause of this newfound happiness…and how long can it last?

“Wolverine: Origin was foundational. It did not simply tell us how, why, and where a young, frail Canadian named James Howlett became the super hero we know as Wolverine, it also showed his loss of innocence and his understanding of a cruel and difficult world,” said Jenkins in a statement. “Now, after 25 years, I’m privileged to present this story I have waited over a quarter of a century to tell. Where did Logan go? Which parts of his story were lost to history? What led to the events of Weapon X? The answers are not going to be what you expect.”

Look for Wolverine: Origin III - The Dark Age to hit stores on December 16. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

For more, learn all about the very first Star Wars/Marvel crossover and read up on Marvel's newest symbiote hero, the Amazing Venom .

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: What to Expect at IFA 2026: AI Is the Name of the Game
articles.summary: Not just a trade show; more like a cultural playground.
articles.body:
Editor's Note: This article is sponsored by IFA 2026. It has been updated with key points on August 18.

IFA 2026 is coming back soon and is set to take the world by storm. The event will highlight how “the future is now” in the realms of AI, smart homes, digital health, robotics, and much more. At IFA 2024, IGN was excited to see Acer announce the Nitro Blaze 7, its own contender to Steam Deck OLED and the Asus ROG Ally X. And in 2025, we saw a ton of home tech reveals from the likes of Eufy and Anker, with Eufy's new MarsWalker robot vacs and UV printers, and Anker's new Soundcore Nebula X1 Pro not-so-portable high-end projector. (It comes on wheels and boasts 3,500 ANSI lumens versus its portable Nebula Capsule that hits a max of 300 lumens, with Dolby surround sound to boot.)

That said, there is a lot of excitement in store for IFA this year, and this guide will share exactly what you can expect from the event so far.

IFA is the world’s biggest home and consumer tech event. Happening in Berlin, it hosts some of the world's leading innovative tech brands like Samsung, Acer, Anker, Eufy, Hisense and more, all gathering in one place to show off tons of cool, new, and interesting consumer gadgets and products. There's everything from gaming tech to home tech, and something exciting at every corner, no matter what you're into.

“Artificial intelligence is no longer just a promise,” says Leif Lindner, CEO of IFA Management. “Smart homes are no longer a vision. Digital health is becoming part of everyday life… The future is not waiting somewhere five or 10 years away. It is already in our homes, in our pockets, in our cars, in our health routines.”

AI and digital health is the theme of this year’s IFA, and the show promises to show more of how AI has “stopped being its own category and started becoming the connective tissue underneath everything else.” And yes, this also includes beauty, preventative health tools, connected fitness, wellness tech, and beauty devices, which signal consumers are looking for tech that “supports a more personalized, healthier daily routine.”

Speaking of personalization, last year's event brought in new robots that were very popular amongst attendees, including the KATA Friend AI pet shown below. There are new, impressive robots that people have never seen before at every show, and in nearly every category you can think of. Some are cute like this advanced digital pet, and others are more practical for every day routines and activities, including a stair-climbing robot vacuum or the Acemate Tennis Robot, the world's first AI-powered robot capable of true, real-time play.

Those in attendance or following along will be able to see these shifts and changes from the lens of a global CEO, a retailer, a startup founder, a content creator, a journalist, and a consumer, and it’s one of the few places that allows for these interactions to happen under one roof.

Furthermore, IFA will be more than just a showfloor, as it plans to utilize Sommergarter, the show’s open-air venue, to host BUNT’s electronic set on September 3, Luciano’s rap/hip-hop mix on September 4, Ikkimel & Friends bringing trap, techno, and Berlin club energy on September 5, and live podcast recordings from Mord auf Ex and Wine Wednesday on September 6.

The ICC Berlin, a protected 1979 landmark that has been closed for over a decade, will also reopen for IFA 2026, providing even more ways for attendees to engage and make the most of the opportunities the event offers.

You! But seriously, tech enthusiasts and general shoppers are welcome to attend. The event will have everybody from global owners to creators to startups to retailers in attendance. For more information, check out IFA 2026’s website, as well as the ticket information for BUNT, Luciano, and Ikkimel & Friends.

IGN will be in attendance at IFA 2026 next week and we look forward to seeing what new gadgets will go viral this year.

Adam Bankhurst is a news writer for IGN. You can follow him on Twitter @AdamBankhurst and on Twitch.

articles.title: Director of Marvel’s Wolverine Responds After Extended Gameplay Footage Sparks Backlash
articles.summary: The director of Marvel’s Wolverine, Mike Daly, opened up about the recent backlash toward the game after its extended gameplay showcase drew criticism online.
articles.body:
The director of Marvel’s Wolverine , Mike Daly, opened up about the recent backlash toward the game after its extended gameplay showcase drew criticism online.

Fans got a better look at Insomniac’s upcoming PS5 exclusive earlier this week, which showed off some story beats, character interactions, traversal, combat, and even a boss fight against a Sentinel.

Since the internet is the way it is, this gameplay footage was instantly subject to intense scrutiny, sparking no end of criticism from players online. There’s a bevy of viral posts poking fun at this most recent footage, some of which I’ve included down below.

Logan, remember to use your adamantium vision to sniff out his trail of wolverine™️ particles https://t.co/vTQssKxGA3 — Space ☆ Bruce (@spacebruce) August 13, 2026

Logan, remember to use your adamantium vision to sniff out his trail of wolverine™️ particles https://t.co/vTQssKxGA3

Why does Sabertooth sound exactly like this https://t.co/g8l4uFYUfT pic.twitter.com/a5o46PpcZa — Deacon (@crowdeacon) August 16, 2026

Why does Sabertooth sound exactly like this https://t.co/g8l4uFYUfT pic.twitter.com/a5o46PpcZa

Logan following a red scent trail to catch The Hand was one major talking point among critics (instantly sparking comparisons to the divisive yellow paint that often guides players in modern games), as was a heated argument between Wolverine and Sabertooth (people weren’t happy with the voice acting here) and the aforementioned Sentinel boss fight.

One particularly damning tweet compared footage from this brawl to a boss fight in the 2007 PS2 game Ben 10: Protector of Earth (why is Ben 10 catching strays?), while another bemoaned that it was too similar to the 2009 X-Men Origins game from nearly 20 years ago.

Marvel Wolverine game's Giant Sentinel fight draws Ben 10 comparisons Many spot clear similarities to Ben 10: Protector of Earth, prompting complaints about overused boss designs in action games pic.twitter.com/bR21DsxAd7 — Beebom Gaming (@beebomgaming) August 14, 2026

Marvel Wolverine game's Giant Sentinel fight draws Ben 10 comparisons Many spot clear similarities to Ben 10: Protector of Earth, prompting complaints about overused boss designs in action games pic.twitter.com/bR21DsxAd7

X-Men Origins: Wolverine's Sentinel boss fight was way crazier and more interesting, while Insomniac Games designed a common, dull boss fight in Marvel's Wolverine. X-Men Origins: Wolverine is a 17-year-old game. 💀 pic.twitter.com/fTafQPMTi2 — Raion Sensi (@RaionSensi) August 15, 2026

X-Men Origins: Wolverine's Sentinel boss fight was way crazier and more interesting, while Insomniac Games designed a common, dull boss fight in Marvel's Wolverine. X-Men Origins: Wolverine is a 17-year-old game. 💀 pic.twitter.com/fTafQPMTi2

These criticisms did not go unnoticed. Speaking with TheGamer , director Mike Daly seemed to be at peace with the backlash, even welcoming it as a sign that the studio is doing something right.

In a somewhat concerning admission, Daly said that Insomniac is “pretty used to” these kinds of responses, calling it a “good problem to have” and remarking that such reactions “come with the territory” when making games based on people's favorite superheroes. And while he knows that Insomniac can make a “great game that a lot of people love,” it won’t stop critics from “finding stuff to complain about.”

“I rest easy about this, knowing that our goal for the game wasn't necessarily to accomplish these things that people complain about. Our goal really was to focus completely on making the best game for the character,” Daly said.

IGN also got the chance to sit down with Insomniac for a massive interview all about the game, with insights into combat, hardware performance, and much more. And while the general internet populace seems to feel negatively about what they’ve seen thus far, our hands-on with the game left us with a mostly positive impression.

IGN’s Mitchell Saltzman remarked that Wolverine’s combat “absolutely nails the spirit of Wolverine and is very fundamentally sound,” saying he was “impressed” with what he played, but noted that it’s still unclear if the gameplay will “hold up over the course of the entire campaign.”

Marvel’s Wolverine releases on September 15, 2026 exclusively on PlayStation 5.

articles.title: Steam Frame Seems to Be On the Horizon as Unboxing and Setup Videos Leak Online
articles.summary: After setup videos leaked online, Valve opted to push them out officially.
articles.body:
It seems like Valve may be gearing up to launch the Steam Frame, the third and final piece of hardware it showed us last year , alongside the Steam Machine and Steam Controller . Earlier today, a number of unboxing, setup and other how-to videos for Valve's upcoming next-generation VR headset leaked online via an update to the ARM Steam Client. Valve quickly pulled them down, but not before they were grabbed and re-uploaded by users.

Instead of pitching a fit – I'm sure the company was not psyched to have these videos leak before originally intended – Valve put the videos back up, and while it hasn't officially pushed them out yet, they're easily found in the Steam backend and can be found via the links collected here .

STEAM FRAME UPDATE: The ARM Steam Client had an update this morning that contained these videos. It was quickly pulled after that, but of course people managed to grab them. These are videos that detail the unboxing, sign-in, and setup of the Steam Frame. pic.twitter.com/AAFk5D69eJ — Steam Hardware Updates (@HardwareSteam) August 19, 2026

STEAM FRAME UPDATE: The ARM Steam Client had an update this morning that contained these videos. It was quickly pulled after that, but of course people managed to grab them. These are videos that detail the unboxing, sign-in, and setup of the Steam Frame. pic.twitter.com/AAFk5D69eJ

The videos detail how to set up and sign in to the device, which will require a Steam account to use. As a reminder, Steam Frame can be used as a standalone VR headset, or wirelessly connected to a PC running Steam. Other videos that leaked include things like how to install the head strap and light blockers, as well as one detailing the wireless adapter and a number of ergonomic accessories.

In his hands-on with the device last year, my colleague Michael Higham noted how Steam Frame gets you the same interface and quality-of-life features as the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, and noted how much he enjoyed using the device as a virtual theater to play non-VR games.

"This kind of experience isn't new," he said, "but the seamless integration through SteamOS also makes it very easy to use, and the super fast wireless tech means you can play PC games with the full strength of your system at low latency."

With these setup videos leaking, it seems likely that Valve is planning to launch the Steam Frame soon, which lines up with the plan to have it in customers' hands before the end of Summer 2026 . That said, we still don't know how much the Steam Frame will cost, but if the price of the Steam Machine (and hardware prices in general ) is any indication, it will likely end up being more expensive than Valve originally hoped .

For more on Steam Frame, check out our Q&A with Valve about why it's going back to VR, how the tech has evolved since the groundbreaking Index VR headset, and how it got wireless streaming to work so well.

Bo Moore is IGN's Senior Manager of Tech. You can find him online @usebomswisely.

articles.title: The Audi S6 Sportback E-tron proves that sedans still matter
articles.summary: Sedans are back!
articles.body: Last year, Audi announced that it gave its all-EV-by-2033 plan the boot, and instead will offer a mix of gasoline, hybrid, and electrified propulsion. There’s no doubt still some uncertainty among bigger automakers — especially those under the Volkswagen Group umbrella — when it comes to such a (now prior) commitment. Even so, what it’s currently offering on the EV front is rather good, and fits into the German brand’s under-the-radar fast sedan tradition quite well. I recently discovered this in the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback E-tron. A cross between a sedan and a wagon in terms of its rearward shape, there’s no hulking Quattro all-wheel drive system to mess with chassis balance, just a motor on each axle, big battery in the middle, massive power output, and solid chassis tuning. Starting at $80,895, here’s how this electrified fast sedan formula shines. The Audi S6 Sportback E-tron rolls out with 800V architecture and a 100kWh (94.4kWh net) battery. Peak power is rated at 543hp and primarily comes from the rear motor, which enables a rip to 60mph in 3.7 seconds. Audi says it’ll charge from 10 to 80 percent in as little as 21 minutes, or 11.5 hours if it’s plugged into a 240V level 2 setup where juice is fed at 9.6kW. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson12.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson5.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson6.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson10.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson11.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson13.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson14.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Peak range is rated at 326 miles; by comparison, the comparable BMW i5 M60 will travel around 45 fewer miles, possesses 50 more hp, runs a similar 0–60 time, and costs a few grand more. During my stint in the Audi, I traveled 295 miles at an average of 2.4 miles per kWh, meaning I saw just 226.56 miles of range. A mighty difference, though; my average speed was just 19mph thanks to much of my driving staying within the Los Angeles basin, plus a handful of highway and mountain-road blasts thrown in for good measure. Much to my surprise, I saw its 270kW peak charging rate at my local Electrify America station during one visit, then as much as 194kW during another. For maximizing charge, the S6 has three levels of regenerative braking: Two are toggled via paddle shifters, whereas full-on one-pedal driving (OPD) is done by putting it in B mode. All three felt smooth, and OPD was just right; not too aggressive and able to smoothly slow down and stop in normal daily driving with ease. The S6’s seats and driving position were quite good, though rear-seat passengers may feel squished due to the Sportback body’s sloping roofline. Cargo volume starts at 26 cubic feet and maxes out at 39, and its large hatch makes loading and unloading easy. The lion’s share of my tester’s $13,595 in options mostly pertained to its added luxury and tech, like more luxurious Audi exclusive interior materials, plus a detailed heads-up display, upgraded exterior lighting, and a screen for the front passenger. Otherwise, the driver has access to Audi’s latest MMI via 14.5-inch center infotainment screen that’s a lag-free and easy-to-swipe-through experience. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson8.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson15.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson16.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson9.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson19.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson20.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson17.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/2027AudiS6SportbacketronPeterNelson18.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Multi-link suspension with sport-tuned air suspension is standard on the S6 E-tron, as are 20-inch wheels with all-season tires. My tester sported the $2,000 Black Optic package, which gives it 21s with grippy Michelin summer tires — though there’s a good chance these knock a few miles off of its EPA-estimated range. Whether in the damper assemblies’ Comfort or Dynamic setting, ride quality was quite good over LA’s most brutal streets, and speed bumps were dealt with particularly well. The even firmer Dynamic Plus was solid and surprisingly agreeable, too. Squeaks and rattles over such cursed surfaces were negligible, though the same can’t be said for driveway clearance scrapes — luckily, there’s some reassuringly substantial plastic on the underside of the front bumper. But the real test came on LA’s freeway system, as that’s where any good fast German sedan should flourish — and the S6 did just that. Wind noise was virtually nonexistent, and it felt very well planted and confident. (It ought to be for weighing over 5,200 pounds.) In town, steering was too light, albeit nicely direct in its response, and thankfully it became more weighted at highway speed. The S6’s 16.4:1 steering ratio was well matched for its size and heft, and it never felt too darty while making split-second lane changes. It may be down on power compared to its BMW rival, but its numbers were still more than ample and its progressive powerband instilled confidence. Going way beyond the speed limit bolstered this confidence even further. Then, on the winding roads of Angeles National Forest just north of Los Angeles, the S6 behaved particularly well. Due to its chassis balance and rear-biased power output, there was never any inkling of understeer, which is characteristic among many Audis of yore. Its tires gripped up well and body roll was basically nonexistent in particularly lateral-G-heavy corners. With traction / stability control shut off, all signs pointed to the S6 being able to exhibit legitimately fun oversteer, which is a welcome trait. If only I could revisit such enthusiasm on a local racetrack. Finally, its brakes don’t look like much compared to rest of this hefty sedan’s dimensions, but they capably shaved off speed, especially with B mode aiding in the effort. Audi’s proven that the luxurious and fast German sports sedan formula applies to EVs, too, in the latest S6 Sportback E-tron. Over 300 miles of range (ideally) and good charging speed is a solid starting point, and its overall balance of comfort and athleticism makes it one of the best big fast sedans that I’ve ever driven.

articles.title: IDW Reveals a Bold, Colorful Future for The Twilight Zone
articles.summary: IDW's The Twilight Zone series has been extended for another story arc, and we've got an exclusive look at these stunningly colorful new sci-fi tales.
articles.body:
In 2025, IDW Publishing added a big gun to its IDW Dark imprint with the debut of a new The Twilight Zone series. Recently, the publisher revealed that the series has been extended for a new batch of six issues (taking the series up through issue #16), and IGN is pleased to be able to reveal new details and artwork from these upcoming books.

Check out the slideshow gallery below to see cover art for The Twilight Zone #11-14:

IDW's The Twilight Zone #11-16 Cover Art Gallery

True to the format of the classic TV series, each new issue of The Twilight Zone will feature a standalone tale from a different creative team. These new issues will feature a common thread, however, as each is presented in limited color rather than the traditional black-and-white. Each issue will feature one specific hue - green for #11, purple for #12, orange for #13, red for #14, yellow for #15, and blue for #16.

"This next volume of the Twilight Zone paints the human spirit in technicolor," co-editors Nic Niño & Ellen Boener tell IGN. "In stories ranging from extraterrestrial to intimately human, we face man-eating plants, giants, funeral rites, and family tragedy… Each cartoonist is taking full advantage of the color in their issue and never in the way you would expect! It’s changed the way artists approach the page; with everyone submitting career-best work."

Look for The Twilight Zone #11 to hit stores on October 21. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

articles.title: The Strange New Worlds Puppet Episode Feels Like It Got Here 20 Years Too Late
articles.summary: The puppet episode of Strange New Worlds feels like it got here 20 years too late, with Ethan Peck’s non-puppet Spock standing tall as the hour’s saving grace.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 5, “Level Five Transporter Accident.”

Alright then, the puppet episode is finally here.

We’ve known this one was coming ever since it was first teased, what, two San Diego Comic-Cons ago ? The latest in high-concept Strange New Worlds episodes – this directly follows the zany Hangover riff from two weeks ago, and last week’s film noir homage – “Level Five Transporter Accident” certainly does feel like an accident… but not one that can be fixed with mere needle and thread the way the puppets here can. Indeed, its only saving grace is the performance from the always reliable Ethan Peck as Spock, who manages to walk the line between comedic Vulcan acting and conflicted Vulcan acting just fine.

When Scotty (Martin Quinn) tries to push his transporter tech to its limits – a nice nod to the Kelvinverse movies, where that Scotty (Simon Pegg) makes some big leaps with the old beam ‘em up technology – things go awry. Since he’s using his childhood puppet “Little Ricky” as a test subject, when the system gets screwy, somehow everyone onboard winds up beaming into puppet versions of themselves. And mostly annoying puppets at that.

I’ve complained about this before, but one of my issues with these Strange New Worlds concept episodes is that a lot of said concepts have been done before, if not ad infinitum , on other shows. The musical episode “Subspace Rhapsody” was great and all, but you know, not exactly an original idea . A film noir episode? Been there. LARPing with the crew? Mmmhmmm . And now we get a puppet episode, the idea of which I can recall seeing at least as far back as on Angel 22 years ago, when it felt like a new idea .

And look, there’s nothing wrong with recycling old premises, but if you’re gonna do it, you gotta bring something new to the table. It’s got to work, and “Level Five Transporter Accident” mostly doesn’t. For starters, by its very nature, the notion of having most of your cast turn into puppets is going to bring a heightened sense of absurdity to things; the characters even harness this idea in their quest to defeat the nasty if forgettable Orion villains of the week. But there’s something about suddenly hearing voices like Anson Mount’s and Christina Chong’s coming from the puppets that I found too jarring. It’s all supposed to be fun and funny, but it’s mostly not, and once again Mount’s take on Pike veers into “this is not a Starfleet captain” territory, wool stuffing notwithstanding.

So what does work here? I think I laughed out loud twice, and both times it was involving the guy at the navigation console next to Ortegas (Melissa Navia) who would usually have been a Red Shirt but instead here is just a funny puppet. His wordless panic about the situation is great. And the puppet designs themselves (created by the Jim Henson Company) are really nice – like, they should sell them on the Paramount+ store because people would want to collect them all. Oh, and the shots near the end of the episode, with the crew all floating around in space in puppet form, are just quite sweet (and really, is how the hour should’ve ended, instead of turning it into an “It was all a dream” scenario for some reason).

And then there’s the Spock stuff, which saves the episode from disaster. Peck’s comedic timing is notable, as he has to run around doing everyone’s jobs for them to keep the ship running, since their little puppet fingers are mostly useless. The actor really has mastered Spock – he and Mount have been playing these characters since 2019 at this point, when they debuted on Star Trek: Discovery – and he always rolls with the various curveballs the writers have thrown at him. Too Vulcan, too human, too Vulcan/human, he’s done it all, and here he’s dealing with not just getting dumped by another crewmate (though La’an was pretty graceful in the dumping, unlike Chapel previously), but also in having to go to his ex, T’Pring (Gia Sandhu), for help in the aftermath of the incident onboard the Griffin earlier this season. I’m glad to see they didn’t just drop that thread, and continuing to explore its impact on both Spock and La’an is welcome.

Questions and Notes from the Q Continuum:

About it all being a dream… was it? Little Ricky sure seemed malevolent in that last shot… or maybe Spock just needs more logic training.

But what is this “studying logic” thing anyway? Hasn’t Spock been doing that since he was in diapers?

Could Little Ricky be a reference to the onscreen son of Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz from I Love Lucy? The puppet even has a red crop of hair on its head. Don’t forget, the pair’s production company Desilu was behind the original Star Trek series.

Pelia (Carol Kane) pointing out that they shouldn’t be able to hear each other in space and how it doesn’t even make sense is an appreciated jab at the grumps in the audience like me.

articles.title: New Fallout Funko Pops Are Dropping in November, Including Vault Boy, Nuka-Girl, and More
articles.summary: Preorders have dropped for new Fallout Funko Pop figures, which are set to be released this November. Priced at $14.99 a piece, here's where you can secure each figure.
articles.body:
Funko Pop is unleashing some new Fallout figures into the wild this year: Vault Boy , Nuka-Girl , Cappy , and Bottle . Priced at $14.99 a piece, each of these is set to be released in just a few months on November 22, just in time for the holiday season. If you're a big fan of the games (or maybe fell in love with them while watching the TV show ), these look well worth picking up to add to your collectibles.

As is the case with most Funko Pop figures, these are all fairly small (around 3.75 inches tall), so will slot nicely into an existing collection of Fallout-themed goodies. They each have quite fun designs as well.

While Cappy and Bottle are just happily posed with waving hands and big smiles, Nuka-Girl is pictured blasting off in a spacesuit with a ray gun, and Vault Boy is modeled with a classic thumbs up pose and a wink. The latter is a slightly different pose to the Vault Boy Funko Pop that released last year for the TV show , as that one was all wide-eyed smiles while posing instead of the wink.

While their release date isn't until late in November, it's worth preordering these now if one or more of them have caught your eye, rather than waiting. These kinds of figures can sell out faster than you'd think, so it's always a good idea to secure your favorites now before stock is all sold out.

If you're looking for even more Fallout items to buy for your shelves, we've got your covered. Our rundown of the best Fallout gear and collectibles highlights some of our favorite finds we think are worth your time, but the IGN Store is also chock-full of Fallout collectibles to look through. articles.title: Best Buy Is Offering a Free $10 Gift Card With These Game Preorders
articles.summary: Best Buy is the only retailer offering a free $10 gift card as a preorder bonus on some of the biggest games coming this Fall.
articles.body:
I’ve been covering deals long enough to remember the good old days when Amazon and Best Buy offered preorder discounts on every video game they sold. Those days are over, but Best Buy is bringing back the spirit of the deal. Right now, when you preorder select games (including The Blood of Dawnwalker), you’ll get a free $10 Best Buy digital gift card at launch. That’s the best (and only) deal going on most of these games. Let’s take a look at the current offerings.

Free $10 Gift Card When You Preorder These Games

The Blood of Dawnwalker (PS5, XSX) + $10 Gift Card

Ace Combat: Wings of Theve (PS5, XSX) + $10 Gift Card

EA Sports FC 27 (PS5, XSX, Switch 2) + $10 Gift Card

EA Sports NHL 27 (PS5, XSX) + $10 Gift Card

So what games are we talking about, specifically? Four games currently qualify for the deal: The Blood of Dawnwalker, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, FC 27, and NHL 27. With the price of games going up to as high as $80 this console generation ( thanks, Nintendo ), I’ll take any preorder discount I can get on games I know I’m going to buy at launch.

The Blood of Dawnwalker comes out September 3. It’s an open-world action-RPG from some of the creative minds behind The Witcher 3 – which is about the most compelling thing you could tell me about any game. It’s set in 14th-century Europe, when powerful vampires have taken over a city in the Carpathian Mountains. You play as a Dawnwalker, a human by day and vampire by night, who fights to take back control of the region. Check out our hands-on preview for a whole lot more info.

Those who enjoy performing aerial combat maneuvers can hop in a digital jet on either September 29 or October 2, depending on which edition you choose. Either way, you’ll go on military missions to take part in dogfights, drop bombs, deploy missiles, and all that good stuff. See our preview for more.

EA might not have the FIFA license anymore, but that hasn’t stopped them from releasing an annual soccer - er, football — game. This year’s edition promises “ultrarealistic” soccer action as well as a new Clubs experience called The Grounds, which lets you “meet, play, and recruit new Club members while competing across a variety of football activities.” Note that The Grounds is not available on last-gen platforms. And click over to our preview to learn more of what to expect.

Fans of ice skating and blasting pucks across the rink can pick up NHL 27 to get a free $10 gift card. Out on 9/11, this year’s edition features all 32 NHL arenas, along with better crowd graphics and real-world goal songs. Anyone who preorders also gets a player pack, 500 NHL Points, and WOC 2XP Boost.
